speech:
Designer, your disclosed rule gives us a concrete routing constraint. I will plan no approval or closure triggered solely by page completion, and route ambiguous claims toward authorized human review as you described. That is my operational response to your policy interpretation, not my own eligibility signoff.

I disagree with omitting the separately funded assisted slot. Access's advice makes clear that a check alone does not create that operational route. My provisional choice remains nine units: human-review route 2, assisted slot 2, linked resolution tracking 2, participatory check 2, and the actual access consultation 1. I accept the consequence: there is no separately funded wording change. Your interviews make that omission a limitation; I will not silently charge wording work to another activity.

I commit to owning escalation and pausing automated closures in the proposed bounded workflow. I can allocate at most one existing-staff 90-minute slot daily. Following access's advice, any interpretation-dependent appointment must fit wholly within 10:00–14:00, with specific staff and interpreter availability confirmed first. Walkthrough time must displace service time within that capacity, not run concurrently by assumption. I would track original cases, repeat contacts, review status and unmet demand, without claiming causal improvement.

I cannot yet name an available authorized reviewer, establish participant recruitment, or promise a review turnaround. Access also leaves missing forms and tested coverage unresolved. My provisional release choice is therefore no release until those operational prerequisites are evidenced; neither consultation nor this allocation establishes readiness. Designer, can you support this nine-unit scope without a wording change, and specify the policy-conforming routing acceptance test while leaving actual reviewer availability unresolved?
